title: Billy Eckstine's bebop band and Pillars's advice about dancers
summary: He lists the Eckstine band's stars including Parker, Stitt, Monk and Blakey, and advises Eckstine to play dance tunes because nobody could dance.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And later on, Billy Eckstine came in, and he came -- he brought Sarah Vaughan back with him. That was the band with all the jazz stars. (Unintelligible). You know about that. We talked about that. Let's see, Sonny Stitt, Lucky Thompson, Charlie Parker, I can't think of the other --
was in that group, too, wasn't he? Thelonius Monk was a Piano player?
Yes, he was, yes. He was a piano player, Monk, and Tadd Dameron was with him, he was writing. And this boy -- Jazz Messengers, what's his name, the boy that --
No, no, no. They called themselves -- he's a drummer.
Art Blakey was playing drums. Art Blakey -- I'm trying to think what trombone they had. They had --
And the girl playing trombone, too, that came in here, that came in here with Redd Foxx? [Melba Liston]-ed
She played trombone, nice trombone. And was that fellow named Green?

Benny Green. That was the band. And they blew and they blew. And I called Billy Eckstine over, I said, "Billy," I said, "just an idea. You've got a great band here." I said, "If you'll take a suggestion, I'll get you a few stocks, just simple tunes and just play maybe two of them, get them on the floor and dance. Then you play one of those -- something to please the guys, you know what I mean, to wind up the dance, see. And then we get off the floor and then we you start off with these little popular tunes. They'll get up and

dance, see." What was happening, they were guys that playing their horns, man, they loved their horns, were playing -- wasn't nobody dancing. And the people didn't enjoy the music because they didn't know what they was playing, see?
